x: John Leslie Brown, Grandison Road.
John Brown ran almost faultlessly to win his heat in 4m. 51s. In the Final he dropped out when lying fourth.

In the 880 Yards John Brown, off 68, won in 1m. 56s., with Main third, Blunden fourth, and Bishop sixth. In the Two Miles Team we turned out three teams, but Finchley had the measure of us, finishing 1.3 and 4 to win by 7 points (3 to score).
Stan Botwright, looking very fit in his R.A.F. uniform, came along to win the 100 Yards, and young John Brown scored a good double, winning the 880 Yards and 1 Mile.

John Brown also displayed fine form in winning the 1 Mile in impressive style, and is another Junior who should make a name for himself. Dick Norton, who owing to leg trouble has had to forego sprinting for the present, turned out in the Weight and won with a very good effort.

John Brown won the 880 Yards in the fine time of 2m. 5.5s., which beat the time of the Senior half on the same afternoon! Young Heathfield also ran a sterling race to win the 440 Yards in 55.4s., which also beat the Senior match time.
Derrick Burfitt, John Brown and Ken Cuff kept together until about half-way, when Burfitt gradually went away to win a good race from John Brown.

John Brown put in a well-judged finish to win the 880 yards in 2 mins. 9.5 secs. In the One Mile, Derrick Burfitt produced a burst of speed at the finish which nobody could match to win in 4 mins. 39 secs.

John Brown lost his mother and a sister when their home was destroyed, and we extend to him our deepest sympathies. John himself was taken to hospital for a short while as he sustained minor injuries, chiefly cuts.

The half was rather slow, John Brown striding home as he liked over the last lap. The Police had no distance men for the One and Two Miles, so a One Mile was held, with Bob Boyden and Tom Morrell scoring for our hosts.
John Brown, our Southern Junior Half-Mile Champion, has been called away at a most interesting period of his running career and is now at Scarborough.

The chief feature of the race was the forward running of several of the younger school, particularly Stan Eeles who perhaps ran his best race to date—Stan has the makings of a real runner if he will get down to it, Fred Clay, John Brown, Bob Boyden, Norman Walker and Alf Heathfield.

John Brown, who is stationed at Scarborough, gained second place in the Northern Command 880 yard championships. This gained him a place in the N.C. team competing in the Army Championships at Aldershot.
In the County Junior races, the Middlesex event was won by Derrick Burfitt, and in the Surrey races, our single individual runner in the under 21 event, John Brown, finished 5th.

He is now demobbed and spent part of his leave in Switzerland, enjoying some of what are to us now "luxury foods." John Brown, still at Catterick, was in the Services team v. B.A.O.R. in Dusseldorf at the end of September.

Among the middle-distance men, Len Marchant and Willie Nankeville were very much to the fore, and with John Brown and Vic Blowfield showing great promise, we can look forward with confidence to next season.

John Brown was second in the Army 1 Mile Championship, and also represented them in the Inter-Services meeting. The L.C.C. promoted what they termed the London Championships and several of our members gained places in the area meetings, which qualified them to appear at the finals held at the Parliament Hill track.
Len Herbert, the holder, tried vainly to overtake the leader, but had to be content with second place with John Brown, coming down from Catterick, to gain third position.
Marchant and John Brown also competed. Charlie Smart made a gallant effort in the 6 miles on Friday evning and eventually finished fifth in 30 min. 42 secs., thus gaining a standard medal.

JOHN BROWN lost his mother and a sister when their home was destroyed, and we extend to him our deepest sympathies. John himself was taken to hospital for a short while as he sustained minor injuries.
Belgrave Harriers regret to announce the death of John “Jack” Brown who passed away on 24 September in his 84th year. He had spent his last years in a nursing home.
